newsitem.title: USA: "Space Jam" shoots to top of U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Space Jam" shoots to top of U.S. box office.

text.p: Michael Jordan and Bugs Bunny slam-dunked their way to the top of the U.S. box office as their basketball comedy, "Space Jam," earned $29.25 million at the weekend, according to studio estimates released on Sunday.

"Space Jam," which mixes live action and animation, pushed last week's number one, "Ransom," into second with $23.0 million. Barbra Streisand's latest movie, "The Mirror Has Two Faces," opened in a distant third with $12.2 million.

Jordan had better luck in his feature film debut than fellow basketball star Shaquille O'Neal, whose "Kazaam" was a summer flop. "Space Jam" averaged $11,038 from 2,650 screens, the highest average in the top 10.

In "Space Jam," Jordan coaches a team of Looney Tunes characters in a basketball match against alien invaders. Larry Bird, Charles Barkley and Patrick Ewing join Daffy Duck, Elmer Fudd and Porky Pig in the warmly reviewed film. According to a Variety poll of critics in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington DC, 23 liked it seven did not and 13 were mixed.
The movie is released by Warner Bros., a unit of Time Warner Inc..

"Ransom," a Walt Disney Co. thriller in which Mel Gibson plays an airline mogul who turns the tables on his son's kidnappers, fell 33 percent from its opening weekend score of $34.2 million. This weekend, the movie averaged $8,342 from 2,757 screens. Its 10-day gross is $68 million.

Some distance behind in third was "The Mirror Has Two Faces," which Streisand also directed and produced. The romantic comedy/drama is released by Sony Corp.'s Columbia Pictures. Her last movie, 1991's "The Prince Of Tides," opened with $10 million and went on to make $75 million, a Sony spokesman said.

The movie, in which Streisand plays an ugly duckling, was fraught with cost overruns as more than a dozen several members of the cast and crew left the production during its lengthy five-month shoot. Critics were not kind, accusing Streisand of extreme narcissism: the Variety poll showed 12 liked it, 22 did not and seven were mixed.

Slipping one place to fourth was the female bank robber drama, "Set It Off," with $5.8 million. The film, which is released by Time Warner's New Line Cinema, has grossed $7.5 million after 12 days of release.

In fifth with $5.6 million was the MTV-styled "William Shakespeare's Romeo & Juliet." Down from second last weekend, the movie has made $31.6 million after 17 days. It is released by News Corp.'s 20th Century Fox.
